anchor: The model's second boundary system separates knowing from doing
statement: Invariant I-3: SufficientKnowledge != ValidDecision != AuthorizedAction — knowing enough is not deciding; deciding validly is not being allowed to act.

From (K_t, Z_t, G) the selector proposes the next epistemic action and holds no authority (I-2); the goal G shapes what is proposed, never what is admitted or executed. Q17's ruling (from the era when the selector still wore a borrowed divine name) held the role analytical, not transformational; the architecture keeps only the deflated, authority-free role, deferring the naming history to Part I.5.

statement: Every decision is a six-part contract DC(d) = (Pre, Inv, Auth, Post, Temporal, Evidence): preconditions, invariants preserved, the authorization requirement, postconditions, temporal validity, and the evidence the decision rests on. Authorization is a precondition constraint filled via governance, never a processing step a pipeline can perform on its own — a COMPOSITION-grade element, and the model says so.

Authorized action produces new observation, closing the loop back into K_t. The boundary (knowledge informs and never executes) is firmly established and the constitutional side hardens the same line ('the Decision Interlock terminates knowledge flows at recommendation'); the semantics of execution beyond that boundary — what an action is, how effects are attributed back, what failure of an authorized action does to the record — are specified only in parts and remain open (OQ-4).

anchor: The deepest defect the programme ever found — four separate times
statement: A system whose admission machinery is governed by a policy that nothing governs is the deepest defect the programme found, discovered independently four times; the ratified answer is stratification.

Policy-as-content is knowledge content at rest inside K_t (admissible, discussable, revisable like any claim); policy-in-force is the approved, versioned policy that actually governs admission; the change between them is a DECISION under DC, approved through governance (BC_Governance), producing version N -> N+1.

anchor: Invariant I-11 closes the I-1 hole
statement: I-11: no in-force policy -- the AcceptancePolicy and the constitution included -- changes without a governed, versioned approval decision; self-modification of the in-force policy is excluded by construction, not by exhortation. I-11 closes the hole the falsification pass found in I-1: the Knower's ownership now reaches Determination through the governed policy chain instead of stopping short at an unowned policy object.

Four independent appearances of the same failure mode, on both sides of the programme: (1) corpus Step 121 flagged a 'critical governance gap' -- the admission constitution unversioned and unowned; (2) the corpus's freeze decisions modified the model's own rules mid-flight with no governing act; (3) the falsification pass caught the synthesized model repeating the pattern (finding F-1); (4) the conformance pass found the implementation side's Constitution asserting ratification downstream of a stale PROPOSED banner -- the mildest form, later resolved when governance located the actual retrospective ratification act.

anchor: Evidence in the ratified model is structured, not scalar
statement: Evidence carries dependency structure and roles; two invariants -- the only two computationally TESTED rather than read -- govern combination: I-5 (duplicate evidence must not increase confidence; independent corroboration must) and I-6 (dependency resolution precedes aggregation).

anchor: EXP-01: four candidate aggregation operators against seven adversarial properties
statement: Both I-5 and I-6 come from the corpus's one genuine experiment, EXP-01: four candidate aggregation operators (MAX, weighted mean, saturating, Bayesian-like) run against seven adversarial properties on a shared normalized evidence universe. The recorded verdict was negative and precise: no simple scalar operator is sufficient as the epistemic foundation; the strongest single lesson was I-6 -- three apparent pieces of evidence may be one observation and two derived representations, so dependencies must be resolved before anything is combined.

anchor: What the experiment did not do
statement: Two candidates survived all seven listed properties, but survival is not selection: the model deliberately selects no aggregation operator (OQ-3, open by ruling); any implementation claiming 'the KnowledgeOS evidence formula' is claiming something the architecture refuses to claim.

The repository contains a CSV export of the EXP-01 property matrix that disagrees with the experiment's own prose record in three cells. The governance track adjudicated it (GN-27): the prose record prevails -- internally consistent under its own normalization footnote, while the CSV is inconsistent under any single reading and carries no generator or provenance. The CSV is graded unreliable-standalone; the negative verdict is unaffected under either source. Reported because the book's provenance rules require every seam the programme found to be findable.

The constitutional layer arrived at the same prohibition from a different direction: a 'knowledge quality' scalar is a forbidden surrogate (Article 2's failure signature is literally 'Knowledge Quality = 0.87'). One prohibition, two independent derivations -- treated as evidence, while still refusing to call it proof.

A three-status admission ladder governed by an explicit policy: Candidate -> Supported -> Accepted. Transitions form a covering relation -- each status reachable only from its immediate predecessor (I-12); skipping is formally excluded. The Supported -> Accepted transition is named Determination, governed by the AcceptancePolicy, which decides what may be admitted -- a different question from what the evidence supports.

Committed is not a fourth epistemic status; it is a decision-boundary status attached to an Accepted item by authority, under the model's sharpest rule A6: authority determines commitment, not evidential truth. Evidence can make a claim Accepted; only an authorized act can make anyone bound to it. The falsification pass caught the earlier formulation quietly treating Committed as a rung of the same ladder; the ratified repair re-typed it, and the lived governance record enacts exactly this discipline (adoption and authorization as separate human acts).

The ladder answers how far admitted, never in what condition held. The ratified Final Architecture layers the constitutional state vocabulary beside it: REJECTED (failed reasoning preserved, never silently discarded), CONFLICTED (contradictory knowledge coexisting until governed resolution, the conflict record surviving resolution), and the evidence-layer triple UNKNOWN != ABSENT != FALSE. These are not extensions bolted on: the archaeology dated them to the programme's first weeks, before the ladder existed -- inherited from the constitutional side rather than invented to fill the gap.

Its identity is prohibitive: each article forbids a named collapse, and each was failure-tested (remove it, and a named corruption opens). This kernel governs; it does not compute.

anchor: The oldest document and its founding stance
statement: The oldest document in the discovery corpus, dated 2026-08-01, is not about KnowledgeOS at all -- a reconstruction baseline for EKS (the Engineering Knowledge System) -- and opens with the stance that would quietly become the whole programme's method: 'Evidence-first / architecture archaeology ... Reconstruction baseline -- not a target architecture ... no future architecture is implied.'

anchor: KnowledgeOS as neighbor; the hindsight ban
statement: The word 'KnowledgeOS' already appears in the oldest document as a neighbor -- something EKS has a relationship to -- and through the root era (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-22) remains a strategic object among others (meta-models, ontologies, character definitions) being circled and compared, not yet formalized. What must not be read into it: none of the later machinery is 'already there' -- the archaeology's finding AF-002 stops exactly at the stance, not the system, and this book follows it.

anchor: Governance vocabulary as practice before formal model: the double ancestry
statement: The root era contributed vocabulary that later became architecture without knowing it would: 'Proposal,' 'acceptance,' 'authorization' -- the words of the later decision boundary -- appear here first as governance practice, in role-separation research and lifecycle documents, weeks before anything formalized them. When Part III's decision machinery reads like a formalization of good governance habits, that is because, historically, it is one: the archaeology calls it a double ancestry -- practice first, formal model later -- and found no conflict between the two.

One relationship the root era opened and never closed: what exactly EKS is to KnowledgeOS. The corpus asserts the relationship repeatedly and settles it nowhere (OQ-11, still open today). This book inherits the question, not an answer.

The kernel-era corpus (2026-08-22 to 2026-08-25, 170 documents) is a reading programme: take the still-soft idea of a knowledge kernel and pass it through as many disciplined lenses as three days allow -- Navya-Nyaya relation logic, the Bhagavad Gita's knower of the field, statistics (seven pillars, uncertainty and belief revision), Bayesian models of mind, typed mathematical modelling. Each lens was mined for properties a kernel must have, not for doctrine; the repository side's closure ruling would later call this the era's achievement: completely different traditions converged on the same structural problems and did not produce new kernel laws.

anchor: Two arrivals that mattered enormously later
statement: Omega enters on 2026-08-24 -- not in the measure-theory crisis where a reader of Part III might assume it was born, but in the typed-model and Bayesian-mind readings, as the ambient space a mathematical epistemic model quietly presupposes; the crisis, when it came a day later, inherited Omega and then had to dismantle it. The aggregation question -- how pieces of evidence combine, what duplicates and corroboration should do -- arrives here as reading-derived intuition from the statistics lenses, three days before the experiment (EXP-01) that would make two of those intuitions the only TESTED invariants in the architecture.

The era's native product was eight competing kernel formulations -- eight different answers to 'what is the irreducible core?' None was selected; the corpus simply moved on, and the selection that did happen (the eleven articles, I.2) happened on the repository side from different material. The eight stand in the record as the shape of the search space. Coverage honesty is carried from the archaeology: the kernel-era corpus was processed at extraction depth (about one document in twenty read in full), so this book inventories the eight and tells the era's story at the resolution the record supports, with the depth caveat attached rather than hidden.

The era also planted two seeds of later collisions: 'Committed' appears here in an unrelated sense ('what is being committed to' -- the kernel's commitment object), and the Gita reading introduced the cast -- the Knower of the Field, the charioteer, the Lord -- whose naming adventures Part I.5 follows.

anchor: The opening choice and its collapse
statement: On the evening of 2026-08-25 a new corpus opens with a confident question: where should the work concentrate -- measure theory, or the definition of KnowledgeOS itself? The first documents choose mathematics: Knowledge would be a measurable structure, sigma-algebras would carry epistemic states. It lasted roughly a day. The crisis documents of the same phase record the failure honestly: the spaces in question refuse the machinery -- what exactly is measurable when the 'space' is everything an unbounded world could present, what does an observer integrate over when no observer stands outside. The foundation was abandoned -- graded ABANDONED by the archaeology, the first of the programme's great discarded alternatives (ALT-01) -- and the vocabulary turnover that followed was nearly total: the corpus stops speaking measure theory within days and never resumes.

The crisis forced the dismantling of Omega, the inherited ambient space, productively: three different fates for three different roles -- the ideal-reference role was absorbed (eventually into the IdealState-and-contract machinery Part III.2 describes); the unboundedness was dropped, bounded away as a modelling decision; and the whole-space-observation role was inverted into the complement principle X_t != Observed(X_t) that survives as invariant I-7. An assumption of total view became a prohibition of assuming one -- arguably the crisis's finest product.

anchor: OQ-6: the Omega-b record gap, held open
statement: One record gap from this episode is held open deliberately: the dropping of Omega-b happened by disuse, not by act. No document rules it out; the corpus simply stops assuming unboundedness. The programme flagged this as OQ-6 -- a one-line historical annotation would close it -- and the annotation is HELD by ruling. This book therefore reports the drop as what it is: settled in substance, unrecorded in form.

anchor: The crisis set the method for everything after
statement: The crisis also set the method for everything after: when the mathematics failed, the corpus did not lower its standards -- it changed instruments, turning from foundations to questions (the Question series Part I.5 enters), and kept the demand for rigor that measure theory had been recruited for. The instrument was wrong; the appetite was right.

anchor: The Sarathi reading hardens into I-1
statement: After the crisis, the corpus reorganized itself around numbered questions -- how does knowledge change state, who owns the goal, what makes evidence sufficient -- and, in parallel, returned to the Gita lens with new seriousness. The era's great gift to the final architecture is the Sarathi (charioteer) reading: the Knower owns the frame; everything else serves it. Of all the era's images, this is the one that hardened into an invariant (I-1) and survived every later regime unchanged. When Part III.2 says the Knower owns problem, purpose, IdealState, and final authority, it is speaking the formalized residue of this reading.

anchor: The Lord's rougher career: two referents, one name
statement: The Lord had a rougher career: the name enters as the Omega-observer (the one who sees the whole field) and, in other documents, as the selector of action. Two referents, one name. The corpus's own Q17 ruling deflated the second: the Lord is analytical, not transformational -- whatever selects the next epistemic action holds no transformative authority. The role survived (Part III.7's authority-free Proposal selector); the name did not, and the two historical referents were never reconciled. The collision stands in the record as OQ-7: a naming question, book-relevant, architecture-open.

anchor: The morning of 2026-08-27: the Atma-Kernel episode
statement: The programme's most compact episode: the morning of 2026-08-27, 08:51 to 09:38 -- eight documents in forty-seven minutes. Atman in the conceptual model; Atman within our KnowledgeOS theory; Atma and Kernel are the same underlying idea; Atma can be the KnowledgeOS kernel; Human Knower -- Atma; Where we started. A complete hypothesis arc -- the Self as the kernel's true identity -- proposed, elaborated, connected to the Knower, and then nothing. The Step series that began hours later simply proceeds with the formal kernel, neither adopting nor rejecting the identification. No act closes the question.

anchor: Ratified disposition: Atma-Kernel as unresolved historical lens
statement: The ratified architecture gives this episode an explicit disposition rather than an accidental silence: Atma-Kernel is an unresolved historical lens (D-FA-5, OQ-8) -- available to this narrative, assigned no architectural role, closable only by a governance act that has not happened. The book honors both halves: the hypothesis was real and is preserved; the architecture does not carry it.
Cross-references only: OQ-3 (III.5), OQ-7/OQ-8 (I.5), OQ-2 (III.9). The late-and-narrow fact is a weight-of-evidence disclosure, not an open question. None chapter-local.

anchor: The Step series and its mature self-attack habit
statement: The final regime of the discovery corpus (2026-08-27 to 08-28) is the Step series: one hundred fifty-eight numbered steps that built the formal model Part III describes, and, in the same breath, the corpus's habit of attacking its own newest work reached its mature form.

anchor: The hour-long life of IdealState v1
statement: IdealState v1 was introduced at 00:08, broken by its own author's worked example at 00:17, and repaired the same night. The episode is the programme's method in miniature: propose precisely enough to be breakable, break it yourself, keep the repair and the wreckage both.

anchor: The experiment and the largest self-audit
statement: EXP-01 (Part III.5) belongs to this era: four aggregation operators, seven adversarial properties, a negative verdict quoted at its exact strength ('no simple scalar operator is sufficient'), and the dependency-first lesson that became I-6. The corpus's largest self-audit (Step 050: fifty attacks on the kernel's consistency) is equally careful to call itself not a proof. The era's evidential temper -- test hard, claim little -- is the reason the final architecture can show TESTED grades at all.

Step 121 found the self-governing-policy gap first on the formal side: the machinery of admission was governed by a policy that nothing versioned and no one owned ('critical governance gap', the record says). The era's own freeze decisions -- stopping parts of the model mid-flight with no governing act -- were the same disease in behavioral form. The falsification pass would later catch the synthesized model repeating it, and the conformance pass would find its mildest cousin on the repository side. Four sightings; III.8 tells what the ratified architecture did about it.

anchor: What the era did not do: non-decisions and the late-and-narrow finding
statement: The era never selected an aggregation operator; never resolved the Lord name; never adopted or rejected Atma-Kernel; never wrote down the no-skip rule it mostly practiced; and -- the archaeology's sharpest structural finding -- it produced its central concepts late and narrow: the EpistemicContract enters at Steps 023/024; the AcceptancePolicy appears in exactly four documents. The concepts Part III leans on hardest are among the corpus's youngest. Their weight is formal depth and the testing they attracted, not breadth of occurrence -- a fact the reader deserves to weigh, and the final rule requires the book to hand over.
